central_synthesis.pattern: Rainfall-associated expansion is dominated by reactivation of historically used species x site chorus combinations rather than uniform amplification, weak-call-only detection, stop relocation, or de novo acoustic novelty.
central_synthesis.temporal_gate: Increasing rainfall contrast selectively strengthens the use of prior same-SiteID chorus memory in the wetter target direction but not the mirrored drier direction.
central_synthesis.spatial_template: Prior same-species strong-chorus history predicts later wet strong chorus beyond generic site quality, decays with metric distance, and is strongest at the exact physical SiteID.
central_synthesis.temporal_memory: Local chorus memory decays with years since prior strong use; >=4-y memory is strongly suggestive but the formal prefixed route gate was not met.
central_synthesis.generality: The local-memory rule is geographically repeatable across deterministic route halves and every leave-one-state-out fit within NAAMP, even though the magnitude of the raw rainfall effect is heterogeneous among states.
central_synthesis.universality_boundary: This is a NAAMP-domain rule. Cross-continental boundary universality remains unestablished.

full_chorus_activation.interpretation: Rain-associated recruitment includes emergence of full choruses, not only marginal CI1 detections.

spatial_depth.interpretation: The excess footprint is concentrated at third-and-later occupied stops and is carried mainly by CI2-3 chorus activity.

recurrent_incidence_memory.interpretation: Wet-survey apparent novelty overwhelmingly comes from combinations observed elsewhere in the historical route/site record.

local_same_species_targeting.interpretation: Species-specific local history remains much stronger than a generic tendency of the SiteID to support choruses.

spatial_kernel.interpretation: Historical chorus memory is spatially localized and decays continuously with geographic distance.

temporal_kernel.gate_failure_reason: 136 routes < prespecified 200-route minimum despite 433 informative pair x species groups.
temporal_kernel.interpretation: Memory weakens with age. A >=4-y effect is strongly suggestive but not formally classified because the route gate failed.

dormant_memory.interpretation: Observed CI0 surveys can intervene between historical strong chorus and later reactivation, but this remains a gated exploratory suggestion rather than a formal PASS.

forward_minus_reverse_cluster_bootstrap.interpretation: Rain proximity selectively amplifies use of the historical local template beyond generic recurrence.

within_species_interaction.localization: Rain-selective memory interaction is strongest at transition into overlapping CI2 chorus; population-level CI3 activation remains independently supported.

local_memory_rule.interpretation: The historical species x site reactivation rule is substantially more geographically general within NAAMP than the raw rainfall effect.

ecological_interpretation.concise: Recent rain acts as a temporal gate on a historically structured, species-specific spatial chorus template. Previously strong species x SiteID combinations are preferentially reactivated, the tendency decays with both distance and elapsed years, and the rule is geographically repeatable within NAAMP.
ecological_interpretation.what_memory_means: Ecological/acoustic memory means predictive information in historical species x physical-site use. It does not imply cognitive memory, continuous occupancy, or return of the same individuals.
ecological_interpretation.strongest_remaining_uncertainty: The proximal cue converting rain into renewed chorus activity (hydration, water availability, pressure/humidity or other breeding conditions) is not identified.
ecological_interpretation.universality_boundary: The reactivation rule is general within sampled NAAMP geography but has not been replicated as a species x site matrix rule on another continent.
